Bug_Details:
Non-thread safe singletons can result in bad state changes. Eliminate
static singletons if possible by instantiating the object directly. Static
singletons are usually not needed as only a single instance exists anyway.
Other possible fixes are to synchronize the entire method or to use an
[initialize-on-demand holder class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initialization-on-demand_holder_idiom).

Refrain from using the double-checked locking pattern. The Java Memory Model doesn't
guarantee it to work unless the variable is declared as `volatile`, adding an uneeded
performance penalty. [Reference](http://www.cs.umd.edu/~pugh/java/memoryModel/DoubleCheckedLocking.html)

See Effective Java, item 48.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the `getInstance()` method, which returns a new instance of the singleton if it does not exist. However, since the creation of the new instance is not synchronized, two threads can simultaneously enter the `if` block and create two separate instances of the singleton, resulting in a non-thread-safe singleton.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggered the bug by calling the `NonThreadSafeSingleton.getInstance()` method simultaneously from two separate threads, resulting in the creation of two separate instances of the singleton, which violates the thread-safety of the singleton pattern.
